title: A Very Easy Target

source.title: Vance 'privately' blasts Netanyahu as Iran war divides Trump administration and 2028 ambitions loom
source.byline: Emma Bussey (Fox News Digital, breaking news)
source.note: published 11-05 19:49 EST; the 11-06 sweep matched it on 'iran' and 'midterms'. Read in full on 11-08 via the cloud fetch (the .print page, complete, 28 body paragraphs) as paragraph reductions, no quotation over ten words. One outside reader (Sachs, MEI) carries fourteen of the twenty-eight paragraphs; the office's post is a later sighting (the fourth page to carry it). Left in the 11-06 queue on 11-07 for the Steinhauser page (one Fox cut per day); cut 11-08 as the newest full-text row on the live object from a source not yet cut today

object.label: H1c — the price leg read by the vote, from the RI? corner, two days on: the office's break with the war read as a 2028 play. The war's cost at the vote is conceded as a given on the page (the AP Voter Poll's roughly six in ten against the military action — the one figure; 'has just taken a huge electoral beating'; 'the unpopular war could cost Republicans control of Congress', written after it did) and the cost's owner is moved — onto Netanyahu, 'a very easy target', whom the office can blame 'without saying a bad word about Trump'. The pump is not on the page; the Strait is, once, as the first fundamental of any settlement. The record of the week beneath the frame: the Qatari letter to Rezaei (received, unanswered), Tehran's formal proposal with seven demands (Reuters, Thursday), the White House weighing strikes, pressure or a settlement

zAxis.pos: the war did not cost the vote — the loss has another cause or another owner

object.gear: fast — the vote (weeks to months); the pump absent from the page; the slow gear (dollar, P3) not on any line

transformNote: the holder's promise — diesel 'COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST' (10-11) — is not restated; the holder has no line on the page (he 'held off' on strikes after endorsing Netanyahu, a reported action, ¶7). What the page does to the object is relocate its owner: the war's cost is agreed (six in ten; a huge beating) and the question the page asks is who the office may blame for it. The answer — Netanyahu, never the holder — is the shadow in a new form: not a wrong reading of the price but a wrong address for the cost. The vehicle is 2028 ('about midnight Wednesday' the campaign began)

lines.quote: 'privately' blasts Netanyahu; the war 'divides' the administration; 2028 'looms'
lines.note: THE DOOR — the loss as palace division; the object (the vote's cause) assumed, not named; the vehicle 2028 in the hed
lines.zWhy: a hed about a split over the war takes the war's cost as given

lines.quote: 'wrong on everything' (Axios, 11-04); the war blamed publicly for the defeat; a negotiated settlement over renewed strikes
lines.note: the author's mechanism in the open: the loss → the war → the exit; the private remark is hearsay at one remove
lines.zWhy: the war named as the defeat's cause by the office, relayed without dispute

lines.quote: 'The reason we lost is the war'
lines.note: CONSTITUTIVE — the office's post of 11-04, later sighting (the fourth page on the Press to carry it); not re-filed

lines.quote: 'low-level hostility' is 'beneficial for Vance'; distance from an administration that 'has just taken a huge electoral beating'
lines.note: THE SHADOW MOVES — the cost conceded in a subordinate clause; the line is about positioning
lines.zWhy: a beating conceded; the war's part in it assumed

lines.quote: a faction urging a negotiated end; 'the unpopular war could cost Republicans control of Congress' — according to reports
lines.note: the mechanism again, tense slipped: written two days after the loss as a conditional
lines.zWhy: the war as the cost of Congress, reported as still pending

lines.quote: Netanyahu urged renewed strikes before the midterms; the holder held off after endorsing him
lines.note: the record: the restraint dated to the campaign; the holder's one action on the page
lines.zWhy: strikes withheld before the vote — the vote read as a constraint on the war

lines.quote: the office's concern 'the prospect of overthrowing Iran's government'; Netanyahu's regime-change plan; an air campaign 'may strengthen the regime'
lines.note: the war's aim, not its cost — the right domain, the wrong plane
lines.zWhy: the war's method questioned; its price absent

lines.quote: if Netanyahu goes: stay confrontational, or say 'it was all Netanyahu'; 'a very easy target'; criticize the war 'without saying a bad word about Trump'
lines.note: THE TARGET NAMED — the cost's address proposed: a foreign leader, never the holder; the page's highest line
lines.zWhy: the war's cost owned by someone other than the holder

lines.quote: the AP Voter Poll: roughly six in ten voters said the military action against Iran was the wrong decision
lines.note: THE INSTRUMENT — the one figure on the page; the vote gear's second instrument beside the NBC exit poll on the clockwork
lines.zWhy: six in ten against the war on the day of the vote

lines.quote: 'about midnight Wednesday' the next campaign began; 'breaking with the policy of President Trump' by criticizing only Netanyahu
lines.note: THE VEHICLE — 2028 dated to the hour; the break sized as a break with the policy, not with the man
lines.zWhy: the loss as the start of the next race

lines.quote: last month, a letter via Qatar to Rezaei (SNSC) proposing renewed talks; the nuclear program the condition (Axios); a US official: the holder backed it; Rezaei: received, not answered
lines.note: the channel dated — the office's instrument for the exit; the holder behind it
lines.zWhy: the exit sought before the vote through a back channel

lines.quote: 'operating on behalf of Trump'; appointed 'in the first few weeks' to negotiate an exit; the MOU gave 'quite a bit to the Iranians'
lines.note: the exit as the office's brief from the holder — the reader's reading of the record
lines.zWhy: the war's end as the holder's own assignment

lines.quote: the White House weighs resumed strikes, pressure, or a settlement; Tehran's formal nuclear proposal via Qatar (Reuters, Thursday), conditioned on seven demands
lines.note: the record of the week — the talks' state as of 11-05; the seven demands unnamed
lines.zWhy: the war's next move undecided two days after the vote

lines.quote: the fundamentals, 'starting with freedom of navigation in the Straits of Hormuz' and a cessation of hostilities
lines.note: THE STRAIT — the only line on the page that touches the pump's cause; the price itself never appears
lines.zWhy: the Strait named as the first term of any settlement

lines.quote: a 'balancing act': distancing from a war he 'was against, so it would seem' while serving in the administration that launched it; 'very difficult… electorally'
